title: Cognitive Exhaust Fumes, or: Read-Only AI Is Underrated — Šimon Podhajský, Head of AI, Waypoint
talk_summary: Šimon Podhajský describes a personal, deliberately read-only AI system that ingests six private data sources and produces cross-source analyses (weekly reflection, who-to-talk-to suggestions) into a separate review vault, never writing back. The core argument is that read-only observers are a distinct product category from acting agents because read errors cost nothing while write errors are unbounded, and because write access contaminates the data being observed.

takeaways.technique: Read-only analysis zone with separate output sink
takeaways.what_they_do: Sources are mounted read-only; the AI never writes back to them, and all outputs land in a separate vault/system for human review before any action.
takeaways.evidence_quote: The sources are read-only. The AI never writes back to them. The workspace is where the analysis happens.

takeaways.what_they_do: Treats observer agents and acting agents as different tool categories rather than maturity levels, assigning read-only observation work to agents whose errors are cheap.
takeaways.evidence_quote: The downside of a read-only error is zero. I just ignore it. The downside of a write error is unbounded.

takeaways.what_they_do: Because observer outputs are only suggestions a human reviews, errors are tolerable, so the analysis can run on whatever model is cheapest without gating.
takeaways.evidence_quote: The observer produces more value per interaction by a wide margin.

takeaways.technique: Clean-session isolation for heavy cross-source queries
takeaways.what_they_do: Runs token-heavy cross-source queries in a fresh session and clears context afterward rather than mixing them into an ongoing session.
takeaways.evidence_quote: this takes up a lot of tokens in the context window, so you probably don't want to do this in a session that is not clean

takeaways.technique: Explicit threat-model note per agent (lethal trifecta)
takeaways.what_they_do: Documents which of private data / untrusted content / external comms each system touches and accepts named residual risk rather than claiming safety.
takeaways.evidence_quote: The worst security posture is the one you haven't examined.
